title: Is the peak too late to vaccinate?
hook: The epidemic has peaked. Does protecting people now still change the ending?

knows: the SIR picture: susceptible, sick, recovered
an unchecked epidemic peaks and then declines
doesNotKnow: that at the peak many people have still never been infected
that protecting people at the peak still removes much of the remaining spread

misconception: Vaccinating after the peak (or at it) is pointless.
objective: The learner can explain that the peak is the middle of an epidemic: about a third of the town is still uninfected, so in this toy model vaccinating 20% of the town from those people at the peak keeps about 78% of the benefit of vaccinating on day 0.

claims.text: In the stage's toy SIR model (R0 = 3, 0.1% sick on day 0), with no vaccination 94% are eventually infected and new cases peak on day 19.
claims.source: Deterministic SIR, Euler step 0.01 day to day 200 (infection 0.6/day, recovery 0.2/day), replicated in artifacts/scratch/w3life/vacc.mjs: ever infected 0.9407, peak at day 19.19. No random seed. | v5 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14, learner r8 / W-298, phone fit): reveal sentence reworded ('Your Seen row: with no vaccine 94% are infected in the end; day 0 brings that to 70%, the peak to 76%.'). Numbers unchanged. Unverified because the text changed.

claims.text: Vaccinating 20% of the town at once, all people not yet infected, brings the final infected share to 70% on day 0 and 76% at the peak (day 19), against 94% with no vaccine: in the stage's whole percents the peak saves 18 of the 24 points that day 0 saves, about 75% of the benefit (unrounded 18.4 of 23.8, 77.5%). On day 40 the final share is 94%. (Stage: 'Seen, infected in the end: none 94% · day 0 70% · day 19 76% · day 40 94% · ...'; day 40 stays in the row once visited.)
claims.source: artifacts/scratch/w3life/vacc.mjs (mode 'sus'): day 0 0.7031, day 19 0.7566, day 40 0.9359, none 0.9407; fraction 0.775. The brief's check (50%, 56%, 87%) did not reproduce in this model; see company/reviews/vaccinate-at-the-peak/build.md. | Builder revision v4 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14): (r7) The reveal now does its arithmetic in the stage's rounding: whole(0.94) - whole(0.76) = 18, whole(0.94) - whole(0.70) = 24, round(100 x 18 / 24) = 75. A Seen row keeps the quoted finals. Builder node re-run of simulate(): none 94%, day 0 70%, day 19 76%, day 40 94%. Builder statement, not self-verified. | FC pass 26 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Own node port of simulate(): none 0.9407, day 0 0.7031, peak day round(19.19) = 19 0.7566, day 40 0.9359; whole percents 94, 70, 76, 94; 94 - 76 = 18, 94 - 70 = 24, round(100·18/24) = 75; unrounded 18.41 of 23.75 points = 0.775. Seen row lists none always, day 0 and day 19 once their milestones are hit (both needed for the reveal); peak clause "Day 19: 35% not yet infected." | v5 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14, learner r8 / W-298, phone fit): the Seen row now keeps 'day 40 94%' once visited, as well as the last other date (r8 minor finding 2). Unverified because the stage behaviour changed.

claims.text: On day 19, the peak, about 35% of the town has never been infected; the peak comes when the susceptible share falls to 1/R0.
claims.source: dI/dt = (beta S - gamma) I = 0 at S = 1/3 (peak at day 19.19); S at day 19 = 0.3455 in the same run. DISPUTED 2026-10-13: Numbers right (S at day 19 = 34.5%; peak at S=1/R0) but the reveal says 'most infections were still to come' at the peak. node: at day 19, 65.5% of the town has already been infected; only 28.6 points remain, 30% of the eventual 94%. So most infections have already happened. Fix: 'about a third of the town had never been infected' or 'nearly a third of the town was still to be infected', and drop 'most' and 'the middle of the epidemic'. | CLAIM FIX 2026-10-13: Was '... so most of the epidemic's remaining infections are still to come' (disputed: 65.5% of the town has already been infected by day 19). Dropped 'most infections still to come' and 'the middle of the epidemic' from the reveal. | v5 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14, learner r8 / W-298, phone fit): reveal sentence reworded ('The peak is not the end: on day 19, 35% had never been infected. Protecting them still cuts the tail; by day 40 little is left to stop.'). Unverified because the text changed.

claims.text: If the 20% of doses went to random people (some already infected or recovered) instead of only to people not yet infected, vaccinating at the peak would keep only about 29% of the day-0 benefit.
claims.source: artifacts/scratch/w3life/vacc.mjs (mode 'random', doses = 0.2 x S): day 0 0.7034, day 19 0.8727, fraction 0.286. Disclosed in the reveal because the lesson's headline depends on the targeting assumption. | v5 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14, learner r8 / W-298, phone fit): withdrawn: the reveal clause 'Given to random people instead, the peak keeps about 29%.' was cut (told context, never on the stage; named as a candidate by the r8 review; 90-word budget). Cutting a claimed sentence is cm-life's call (board).

claims.text: The model is a made-up disease with random mixing, instant and perfect protection, and doses only to people not yet infected (the question says 'all not yet infected'; the reveal says 'Model, not guidance: instant, perfect protection.'); it is a model result, not guidance.
claims.source: Model choice in Demo.tsx; stated in the question, on the stage ('Toy: ... all not yet infected') and in the reveal. | v5 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14, learner r8 / W-298, phone fit): muted reveal line shortened to 'Model, not guidance: instant, perfect protection.' ('doses only to people not yet infected' cut: the question already says 'all not yet infected'). Unverified because the text changed; cm-life to confirm the cut.

claims.text: R0 = 3 means that, early on, each sick person infects 3 others on average; in the toy model infection 0.6 per day over recovery 0.2 per day gives exactly 3.
claims.source: R0 = beta/gamma = 0.6/0.2 = 3 in the SIR model (Kermack and McKendrick 1927). Demo shows it rounded because floating point gives 2.9999999999999996. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 11): R0 = beta/gamma for SIR; 0.6/0.2 in node = 2.9999999999999996, Demo.tsx rounds to 3 (line 18).

claims.text: From day 23 on, fewer than 20% of the town are still not yet infected, so the dose is capped at what is left: on day 40 only 6% are not yet infected, so only 6% can be vaccinated. (Stage line: 'Day 40 (after the peak): only 6% not yet infected, so only 6% vaccinated. Final: 94% infected.')
claims.source: Demo.tsx simulate(): v = min(DOSE, S) at the vaccination day. Builder node re-run (2026-10-14): first day with S < 0.2 is day 23 (S = 17.57%); day 40 S = 6.41%, vaccinated 6.41%, final 94%. Builder statement, not self-verified. | FC pass 26 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Own node: S at day 22 = 20.49%, day 23 = 17.57%; S only falls, so every day from 23 to 60 is capped (vax < DOSE) and gets the capped line. Day 40: S = vaccinated = 6.41%, final 93.6%; the generated line is exactly "Day 40 (after the peak): only 6% not yet infected, so only 6% vaccinated. Final: 94% infected."

recall.question: In a simple well-mixed epidemic model with no interventions, roughly where is the epidemic when new cases peak?
options: Nearly over: almost everyone has been infected
Around the middle: many people have never been infected and many infections are still to come
Just starting: almost nobody has been infected
recall.why: The peak comes when the susceptible share falls to 1/R0; with R0 = 3 a third of people are still uninfected, so protecting them still changes the ending.
